summary: The new fact that decides this round is probe 45: exp70g (K2 + DaughterNet insertion cap 6) = 0.956 (#268 -> #162; CONTEXT 27 Sep 18:56Z). The exp60 lab had vetoed it (pooled -0.00057; its 85 extra insertions were 0 TP / 4 FP / 81 unannotated). Round 15 upheld the closure ('upper bound <= +0.0009, central ~0'). This is the second time a division knob has read with opposite signs in the lab and on the public LB, after DC 0.30 (lab +0.0010 on 6bba, public -0.005). Both flips point the same way: the lab under-values forks on the public embryo. Three re-checks follow. (A) The insertion-volume closure is FALSIFIED and REVIVED as the lead public lever. It covers the I-066/I-067 grid and cap, the R15-RC-A upheld verdict and round 18's rejection of exp73s/c. Dummy anatomy shows three things. The cap 4 -> 6 increment was 100% orphan insertions, and the steal cap never binds. DaughterNet cost does not depend on the cap or the threshold. Cap 8 already exhausts the eligible pool on sparse clips, so THRESH is a separate axis that reaches clips the cap cannot. (B) Four division-ADD families were killed on lab precision: I-077 mirror/lowdet daughter, I-078 edge-evidence daughter, I-076 DC-rejected rescue and I-063 DaughterNet v2 ranker. Their premise is broken, but they STAY CLOSED for 29 Sep: they need new code or new weights, R8 applies, there is no honest gate and there are no local v2 weights. They go to the top of the post-deadline list. (C) The finals rule 'keep #38 whenever the partner carries the insertion' (R12-A3, R14-RC-C) is OBSOLETE once F1 carries cap >= 6. By the E[max] algebra, #37 is the better partner exactly when the cap increment hurts private, and #38 only when the whole insertion hurts. At cap 6 the two partners are a wash (~1e-4). As F1's cap rises, #37 dominates. This supports the session's option A {exp70g, #37} for the user's 29 Sep pick. Nothing was submitted, pushed or committed. The only files written are research/wf_ideas_v4/round20/scan_recheck.json and scan_recheck.notes.md.

findings.what: Insertion volume knobs: DIVINS_CAP beyond 4, FRAME_CAP and THRESH (I-066 144-config grid and budget ladder; I-067 cap beyond 4; round 18's 'exp73s/c OUT'). OLD VERDICT: closed, for four reasons. (1) v3 said '~5 evaluable public forks; |delta| <= 0.0015; the LB cannot see it; precision falls with rank'. (2) In v2, cap 4 -> 6 on SELECTION gave 0 TP / +2 FP. (3) The 26 Sep 21:56Z lab rule measured cap 6 at -0.00057 pooled (44b6 -0.00079, 6bba -0.00052; its 85 extra insertions were 0 TP / 4 FP / 81 unannotated), so exp70g was not sent in the 00:05Z slot. (4) R15-RC-A upheld the closure ('upper bound <= +0.0009 public, central ~0'). Round 18 then dropped exp73s/c on the lab plus amanatar V6. WHAT CHANGED: probe 45 exp70g = 0.956, against 0.954 for #37 (the same K2 at cap 4). The true delta is in (+0.001, +0.003), so it exceeds the R15 upper bound and the lab sign was wrong. The V6 half of round 18's reason had already been retracted as mis-attributed (R19-RC-C). NEW EVIDENCE from the dummy run_stats.csv, 4 clips (44b6_0113 / 44b6_0b24 / 6bba_05b6 / 6bba_05db): (a) Eligible insertions at thr 0.4: 14 / 0 / 33 / 142. (b) Added insertions: 4/0/4/4 at cap 4, 6/0/6/6 at cap 6, 7/0/8/8 at cap 8. (c) Steals stay at 2/0/1/2 for caps 4 and 6, and skipped_steal_cap = 0 everywhere. So the 4 -> 6 gain came entirely from ORPHAN insertions (a track start v attached as the second daughter). The steal-cap rise 2 -> 3 is not a confound. (d) At cap 8, 44b6_0113 is exhausted: 7 of 14 used, and the rest are blocked by node reuse. Further cap only acts on dense clips, where FRAME_CAP 1 already blocks 10-11 insertions per clip. (e) exp70q's thr 0.3 raises eligible to 59 / 2 / 42 / 391 and inserts on 44b6_0b24845f, which had 0 eligible at 0.4. THRESH reaches clips that CAP cannot, so it is a separate axis. (f) divins_nodes_scored is identical across cap and thr (3869/6988/661/20770), so the knobs add no DaughterNet runtime. Probe 45 L is in (7.49, 7.67] h, and the 8.0 h insertion gate did not fire. Rough scale (guesses: ~30 public videos, ~1.5 extra insertions per clip, ~3% evaluable). Cap 6 added ~45 public insertions, of which ~1-2 were evaluable. The +0.001..+0.003 equals ~1-2 net division TPs. So at the margin the evaluable public insertions were mostly TPs, where the lab said 0/4. NEW VERDICT: REVIVED as the lead public lever. The lab has no say on the SIGN of division-volume knobs (two flips, both under-valuing forks). The dose curve can only be read on the LB.

findings.what: Division-ADD mechanisms refuted on lab precision: I-077 mirror / low-detection second daughter ('~0.5 TP vs ~1.5 FP on public'); I-078 edge-evidence second daughter ('precision 0.19 < 0.265'); I-076 rescue of DC-rejected forks with image evidence ('precision 4-15%'); I-063 DaughterNet v2 / v1+v2 ranker (R14-RC-B: 'undecided, closed for R8'). OLD VERDICTS: all were priced from lab or in-sample marginal precision. R2-RC-B upheld the closure on in-sample inputs, R4 and R8. WHAT CHANGED: probe 45 shows that, on the public embryo, the marginal insertion forks were net TPs where the lab counted 0 TP / 4 FP. Two more facts point the same way. DC 0.30 read lab +0.0010 against public -0.005. v2 found the public embryo 'division-easier' (J_pub ~0.36 against lab 0.05-0.21). So the premise 'lab precision predicts public or private precision for added forks' is broken. The cheapest member is a v2 ranker swap through the existing BIOHUB_DIVINS_WEIGHTS glob. It also gains value as the cap rises: at cap 8-12 the ranking of marginal candidates matters more, and v2's honest pool AUC is 0.875 against v1's 0.825. NEW VERDICT: the reason is corrected, but they STAY CLOSED for 29 Sep, for four reasons. (a) I-076/I-077/I-078 are new code after R8 and have no dummy. (b) The v2 weights are not local: weights_dataset/vitalii_daughternet holds only v1 fold_0..4.pt, and v2 sits in a Kaggle kdn-train output. v2 would also need a re-mapped ensemble threshold, which counts as a knob neighbour. (c) The lab cannot gate any of them honestly any more, because it mis-signs division adds. (d) A slot spent on them displaces a dose rung, whose public sensitivity is measured. Post-deadline, they go to the top of the list as 'division-add on a division-rich embryo', gated on public-like data (dorado or late submissions), not on the exp60 lab.

findings.what: The finals insertion hedge {#37, #38} (R12-A3). R14-RC-C made it a rule: 'every row keeps #38 whenever the partner carries the insertion; hedge reinforced' (P(insertion < 0 on private) 0.10-0.20). Round 16 R16-A2 kept it as the default pair. WHAT CHANGED: (1) F1 is now a cap >= 6 file: exp70g scored 0.956, and cap 8/12 rungs are coming. (2) The insertion now shows a monotone public dose response: 0.953 (#38, cap 0) -> 0.954 (#37, cap 4) -> 0.956 (cap 6). (3) The lab gives the 4 -> 6 increment a NEGATIVE in-sample sign on BOTH train embryos (-0.0008 / -0.0005). The base insertion is honest-OOF positive on both (+0.0015 / +0.0021, old base). RE-DERIVED E[max]: let x be the private effect of cap 0 -> 4 and y the effect of 4 -> 6. Then max(F1,#37) - max(F1,#38) is: -y (or x) when x > 0 > y; x or x+y (both < 0) when x < 0; and 0 when x and y are both > 0. So #37 is the better F2 exactly when the increment hurts private and the base insertion helps. That is the lab-like private world (P ~0.35-0.5). #38 is better only when the whole insertion hurts (P 0.10-0.20). With |y| ~0.0003-0.0006 and |x| ~0.001-0.002, the two are a wash at cap 6 (~1e-4 either way). As F1's cap rises to 8 or 12, |y| grows and #37 dominates. NEW VERDICT: the rule 'keep #38 whenever the partner carries the insertion' is OBSOLETE for an F1 at cap >= 6. The hedge axis is now insertion VOLUME, and the right F2 is the lowest-volume insertion file, #37. This supports option A {exp70g (or the best cap file), #37}, which the session sent at 19:01Z.
